_comment: Per-block qualifier attribution cases (issue #7). Rules: docs/mining_system.md §7 and §7.1. Expected values recorded independently of any implementation. All BLAKE3 outputs (tie_seed, draw_rank) are FIXTURE-PINNED because canonical_encode's byte layout is not yet specified — see README open question 1. The seed inputs are authoritative; the hex values model the persisted draw artifact that mining_system.md §7.1 requires the pool to store.

context._benchmark_provenance: The snapshot's get-benchmarks.json is empty at the anchor; per docs/tig_integration.md §5.2 bundle qualities come from the incremental active-benchmark metadata cache. The benchmarks below are constructed cache contents, consistent with the snapshot's published qualifier counts above.

cases.name: no_tie_full_groups
cases.description: Challenge c001 track t001: quality groups are accepted whole from highest to lowest; the last group fits the remaining positions exactly (N == M), so no random draw occurs.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §7 steps 1-9 (steps 6-7: accept complete quality groups while enough positions remain; step 8 draw not triggered because no group crosses the boundary)

reconciliation_check.rule: accounting.md §6: stored bundle selections must aggregate to TIG's published pool qualifier count for every challenge and track

cases.name: equal_quality_boundary_draw
cases.description: Challenge c001 track t002: a group of N=3 equal-quality (75) bundles crosses the remaining boundary of M=2 positions. The persisted random seed and the resulting boundary selection are recorded. Draw ranks are fixture-pinned (README open question 1); selection is the M entries with the smallest draw ranks.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §7 step 8 and §7.1 (tie_seed derivation, draw_rank, smallest-M selection, persisted boundary artifact)

persisted_tie_draw._rule: mining_system.md §7.1: store boundary candidates, seed inputs, draw ranks, and selected entries with the block payout

cases.name: draw_rank_collision_identity_tiebreak
cases.description: Challenge c003 track t010: quality-88 entry accepted whole, then a group of N=3 equal-quality (70) bundles crosses M=2 remaining positions. Two candidates have identical fixture-pinned draw ranks; the collision is broken by the canonical bundle identity (benchmark_id, position).
cases.rule: mining_system.md §7.1: 'A hash collision is broken by the canonical bundle identity.'

draw_order_smallest_first._note: bench_c3#1 has the smallest rank; bench_c3#0 and bench_d3#0 collide at 0x77..77, so canonical bundle identity orders (bench_c3, 0) before (bench_d3, 0)

cases.name: zero_published_count
cases.description: Challenge c003 track t011: the pool has an active benchmark with bundle entries, but the published qualifier map has no (c003, t011) entry, which reads as zero positions. No entry is accepted; the member's q contribution is 0.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §7 steps 1 and 7: Q read from OPoW data is 0 (absent key), so no positions remain and no group is accepted

input._note: absent key in num_qualifiers_by_challenge_by_track reads as 0

cases.name: per_member_aggregation
cases.description: Aggregate the accepted entries of every (challenge, track) of block_100080 (cases 1-4) by member to produce the block weight q[m,b] consumed by accounting.md §6. These weights are the input to payouts.json case ordinary_block_exact_division.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §7 step 9; accounting.md §13 invariant 3 (stored member qualifier weights sum to TIG's published pool count)
